Model a composition as an independent variable

Source: R/comp_iv.R
comp_iv.Rd

Fits a model of an outcome on the pivot ILR coordinates of a time-use composition (plus optional covariates), with the model class selected by model. The composition comes entirely from a compD object created by declare_composition(). The coordinates enter linearly, unless curvature = TRUE adds their full quadratic or formula writes other terms.

Usage

comp_iv(
  comp,
  outcome = NULL,
  model = c("lm", "glm", "cox", "coxme", "lmer", "glmer", "clm", "clmm", "mblogit",
    "lmrob", "rlmer"),
  covariates = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  random = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  formula = NULL,
  moderator = NULL,
  curvature = FALSE,
  include_total = FALSE,
  model_args = list()
)

Arguments

comp

A compD object from declare_composition().

outcome

Name of the outcome column in comp$data_raw (not used by model = "cox" or "coxme", which use time/event). A model formula may also be passed here positionally (e.g., comp_iv(cd, y ~ ilr() * sex)), the way lm()/glm() take a formula first; see formula.

model

The fitting engine. comp_iv() wraps established backends, and model takes the backend's own name. Clustered and unclustered variants are separate keys, and random is required by the clustered ones and rejected by the rest. Backends marked Suggests are checked at call time.

"lm", "glm"

stats::lm(), stats::glm().

"cox", "coxme"

Cox proportional hazards models via survival::coxph() and, with a random intercept or other (1 | g) terms, coxme::coxme() (random required). Reports hazard ratios.

"lmer", "glmer"

lme4::lmer(), lme4::glmer(); random required.

"clm", "clmm"

ordered-factor outcome via ordinal::clm() and ordinal::clmm() (random required). Reports cumulative odds ratios.

"mblogit"

unordered-factor outcome via mclogit::mblogit(), optionally clustered through random. Reports one relative-risk ratio per non-reference outcome category, so summary() and predict_realloc() gain a response_level column. For a two-level outcome, a logistic regression with model = "glm" and family = "binomial" reports the effect as an odds ratio. With random, the convergence element of the fit holds mclogit's own convergence flag, which can read as converged although the inner iterations warned. A clustered fit has no log-likelihood.

"lmrob", "rlmer"

robust linear models via robustbase::lmrob() and robustlmm::rlmer() (random required).

"cox", "coxme", "clm", "clmm" and "mblogit" support predict_realloc(type = "relative") only.

covariates

Optional character vector of covariate terms. An interaction between the composition and a covariate (a term involving ilr coordinates) makes reallocation contrasts covariate-conditional; predict_realloc() then needs at or by.

family

A GLM family (object or name, e.g., "binomial"), required for model = "glm" and model = "glmer" and rejected by the other engines. A family given by name is resolved in the calling environment, so a locally defined family function works. Its link must be "identity" (the effect is a mean difference), "log" (a rate ratio for Poisson, a risk ratio for binomial, a ratio of means otherwise) or "logit" (an odds ratio). Any other link, such as binomial(link = "probit") or the default inverse link of stats::Gamma(), is an error.

random

Random-effects specification. A character vector of grouping column names (each expanded to (1 | name)) and/or full lme4 terms (any element containing | is used verbatim), such as random = c("province", "school"). Required by "coxme", "lmer", "glmer", "clmm" and "rlmer", optional for "mblogit", and rejected by the unclustered engines. "mblogit" takes one grouping term, passed as its own random argument: a grouping name gives a random intercept (~ 1 | school), and a bar term keeps its left-hand side ("(ilr1 | school)" gives the random slope ~ ilr1 | school).

time, event

Survival outcome columns for model = "cox" and "coxme": time positive follow-up times, event 1 = event, 0 = censored.

formula

Optional model formula, an alternative to outcome/covariates/random/time/event/moderator for models with further interactions and non-linear terms, fitted as written. It is mutually exclusive with the discrete arguments, moderator and curvature. The left-hand side is the outcome, or a survival::Surv(time, event) call for model = "cox" and "coxme". On the right-hand side, the marker ilr() stands for the composition (expanded to ilr1 + ... + ilr{D-1}), and everything else passes through to the model function, so poly(), splines::ns(), I(), a*b and (1 | g) random terms all work.

Non-linear terms may enter the composition too (ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2), poly(ilr(), 2)), with or without its main effect; ilr() gives the expansion rules and the specifications that depend on the order of the parts. If ilr() is absent, the composition is added as a main effect, even beside coordinate names (ilr1, ...) typed by hand. When ilr() is present but a coordinate's main effect is not, comp_iv() warns that estimates may be biased. A formula fit, even outcome ~ ilr() * x, carries no moderation test and no default by for predict_realloc(); use moderator for those.

A variable the formula names must be a column of the compD data or a scalar in the formula's environment, such as a knots value. A longer object, such as a vector of the caller's, must be a column instead. A scalar is replaced by its value when the model is fitted, and the stored formula holds the value. The expressions in covariates follow the same rule, with or without moderator and curvature; their scalars are found in the environment comp_iv() is called from.

moderator

Optional name of a single covariate to test as a moderator of the composition's effect. It adds the ilr() * moderator interaction, so the fit equals formula = outcome ~ ilr() * moderator (plus any covariates and random terms). Unlike that formula fit, the moderated fit stores the joint Wald test of the moderation in moderation. A factor or character moderator also becomes the default by of predict_realloc(), which then gives one estimate per level. The test identifies the moderator's coefficients by the factor's own contrasts or those set with options(contrasts =); a coding set through the backend's contrasts argument in model_args is not recognized. outcome, time and event follow the same rules as without a moderator. The moderator must not also appear in covariates, and moderator is mutually exclusive with formula.

curvature

Logical (default FALSE). When TRUE, the composition enters as the full quadratic in the ILR coordinates, ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2): the D-1 main effects, every pairwise product and every square, (D-1)(D+2)/2 coefficients. The fit equals the one from formula = outcome ~ ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2) with the same covariates and random terms, and every method reads it as that formula fit. The full quadratic is the same model in every ILR basis; a squares-only term or a spline, which changes with the order of the parts (see ilr()), is written through formula instead. With moderator, the interaction stays on the main effects (ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2) + ilr() * moderator), so moderation tests the same coefficients as without curvature. The joint Wald test of the squares and products is stored as curvature_test. The argument is an error beside formula, which writes its own curvature terms, and when covariates names a coordinate (ilr1, ...) or the ilr() marker, both already held by the quadratic.

include_total

Logical (default FALSE). When TRUE, fits the total-as-covariate model of Coenders et al. (2017), for compositions whose row totals vary (waking hours, dietary intake). The normalized log geometric mean of the zero-free parts on their original, pre-closure scale (the parts_imputed element of the compD), \(t = \sqrt{D}\,\log\big[(x_1 \cdots x_D)^{1/D}\big]\), enters the model as the main effect t_total. The ILR coefficients then estimate the effects of proportional shifts at a constant total, and t_total the effect of scaling every part up proportionally. A (near-)constant total, such as the fixed 1440-minute days of timeuse, is an error. Reallocations hold t_total at total_ref, and the Wald test of t_total is total_test, shown by summary(). The option combines with every engine, covariates, formula, moderator and curvature; t_total itself cannot be named in covariates, formula, moderator or model_args.

model_args

A list(...) of further arguments passed straight to the fitting function of the chosen backend (e.g., model_args = list(weights = w, na.action = stats::na.omit) for stats::glm(), or list(nAGQ = 0) for lme4::glmer()), and the route to any backend argument comp_iv() does not expose itself. The arguments are captured unevaluated, so a bare column name works (weights = w refers to a column of the composition data, exactly as in a direct stats::glm() call) and the fitted object's stored call stays readable. A name that is not a column is found in the environment comp_iv() is called from (with or without moderator), or, with a formula, in that formula's environment.

An engine's own control object goes here too, such as model_args = list(control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")) to retry a mixed fit with a different optimizer, or list(control = stats::glm.control(maxit = 100)). Each backend documents its own arguments, control functions included. An argument the engine already sets (trace for "mblogit", model for "cox", Hess for "clmm") is an error. A link other than "logit" is an error for "clm" and "clmm", whose effects are cumulative odds ratios.

Value

An object of class c("comp_iv", "timecoda_fit"): the timecoda_fit metadata (fitted model, model_type, parts, total, ref_comp, family, ...) augmented with the elements below. family is the resolved GLM family object (class "family", carrying its link) for model = "glm" and "glmer", and NULL for every other engine. The backend object model, like each of models, carries its formula and fitting data in its call. R's own tools therefore re-fit it: stats::update(), stats::drop1() and stats::anova() between two such fits work on it directly for every engine. survival::cox.zph() works on a plain Cox fit (model = "cox"). Current versions of survival do not support it on a "coxme" fit, and it should not be called on one. Printing that object itself (print(fit$model), summary(fit$model)) shows the data inside the call; print() and summary() of the comp_iv() fit do not.

omnibus

A one-row tibble (term, statistic, df, p.value): the joint Wald test that every coefficient of a term in the ILR coordinates alone is zero (i.e., that the composition as a whole has no effect). The statistic is referred to a chi-squared distribution on as many degrees of freedom as there are such coefficients. These are D-1 for the main effects, plus one per square, product or basis column of a non-linear term ((D-1)(D+2)/2 for the full quadratic ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2)), and one set per non-reference category for a multinomial model. A formula with no term in the coordinates alone (ilr():sex) tests every coefficient crossing a coordinate with a covariate instead. Aliased (NA) coefficients, such as a linear term repeated by ilr() + poly(ilr(), 2), are left out of the test and of its degrees of freedom. The test is NA on 0 degrees of freedom when no fixed-effect coefficient carries the composition, for example when it enters only through a random slope (zbmi ~ age + (ilr() | school)). The test is also NA, with a warning, when every composition coefficient is aliased (a composition that is the same on every row, or collinear with another term). For a linear model the statistic equals its degrees of freedom times the F statistic of the same hypothesis. The chi-squared reference ignores the uncertainty in the residual variance, so in small samples the test is slightly anti-conservative, with a p-value a little smaller than that of the exact F test.

comp

The compD object.

models

A named list (one element per part) of the rotated fits: models[[part]] is the model refitted with that part as the first pivot coordinate, so its ilr1 term is the "part vs remaining" effect summarized by summary(). The refits leave the canonical model unchanged, and no prediction path reads them. For a mixed model, one refit per part can be slow.

moderator

The moderator column name (or NULL).

moderation

When moderator is set, a one-row tibble with the joint Wald test that every composition-by-moderator coefficient is zero (H0: no moderation). Its degrees of freedom are (L-1)(D-1) for an L-level factor moderator and D-1 for a numeric one, times K-1 for a multinomial fit with K outcome categories. NULL otherwise.

curvature_test

A one-row tibble when the terms in the ILR coordinates alone are the full quadratic: a square written I(ilrK^2) for every coordinate, a product ilrJ:ilrK for every pair, and no other term above degree one. It is NULL otherwise, including for poly() and spline terms and for a square or product written in another form (such as I(ilr1 * ilr2)). The tibble holds the joint Wald test that every square and product coefficient is zero (H0: the effect is linear in the coordinates). The degrees of freedom are (D-1)D/2, times K-1 for a multinomial fit with K outcome categories, less any aliased coefficient. The test is the same whether the quadratic comes from curvature = TRUE or from a formula, with or without a moderator, and in every ILR basis.

random

The resolved random specification (character vector of grouping terms), or NULL for a non-clustered fit.

fit_warnings

A tibble of the backend warnings/messages captured across the canonical and rotated fits (columns source, type, message; zero rows when every fit was clean). See the Convergence section.

convergence

A one-row tibble (converged, singular, n_warnings) probing the canonical fit's convergence state.

total_test

When include_total = TRUE, a one-row tibble: the Wald test of the t_total coefficient (H0: the total carries no effect beyond the composition), on 1 degree of freedom, or K-1 for a multinomial fit with K outcome categories. NULL otherwise.

total_ref

When include_total = TRUE, the mean of t_total, which is t_total at the geometric-mean composition of the original-scale parts; every reallocation holds t_total at this value. NULL otherwise.

Total as a covariate

The \(\sqrt{D}\) factor makes t_total the coordinate of \(\log x\) along \(\mathbf{1}/\sqrt{D}\), which completes the ILR basis to an orthonormal one (Coenders et al. 2017, eq. 3.2). Any positive rescaling, such as a \(\sqrt{D-1}\) convention, rescales its coefficient inversely and leaves the fit, the predictions and total_test unchanged.

Convergence

Every engine is fitted with its backend warnings and messages captured (and still re-emitted). The fit carries two additive elements: fit_warnings, a tibble of the captured conditions (source, type, message; zero rows when clean) whose source is "canonical" or a rotated part name, and convergence, a one-row tibble (converged, singular, n_warnings). summary() prints the captured messages and, for a clustered or iterative fit, a Convergence: OK line when clean; print() flags the warning count. "cox" and "coxme" fits are not probed (converged is NA), so they print no such line. An "lmer" or "glmer" fit that fails to converge or is singular can be refitted with a different optimizer through model_args (e.g., model_args = list(control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))).

Degrees of freedom for clustered fits

For an "lmer" fit, the per-part standard errors, intervals and p-values that summary() reports and the reallocations of predict_realloc() use the same degrees-of-freedom method, chosen by the rule emmeans applies. The default is the Kenward-Roger approximation through pbkrtest. The Satterthwaite approximation through lmerTest is used when emmeans::emm_options(lmer.df = "satterthwaite") is set, or when pbkrtest is absent, disabled or the fit has more observations than emmeans::emm_options(pbkrtest.limit =) (3000). Both pbkrtest and lmerTest are optional, and when neither can be used, or lmer.df = "asymptotic" is set, the degrees of freedom are asymptotic (normal). "glmer", "cox", "coxme" and "rlmer" fits are asymptotic in both places (robustlmm reports no degrees of freedom), and "lmrob" fits use their residual degrees of freedom.

References

Coenders, G., Martín-Fernández, J. A., & Ferrer-Rosell, B. (2017). When relative and absolute information matter: Compositional predictor with a total in generalized linear models. Statistical Modelling, 17(6), 494-512. doi:10.1177/1471082X17710398

Cox, D. R. (1972). Regression models and life-tables. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 34(2), 187-202. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1972.tb00899.x

Kenward, M. G., & Roger, J. H. (1997). Small sample inference for fixed effects from restricted maximum likelihood. Biometrics, 53(3), 983-997. doi:10.2307/2533558

McCullagh, P. (1980). Regression models for ordinal data. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 42(2), 109-127. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1980.tb01109.x

See also

declare_composition() to build the compD input; summary.comp_iv() and plot.comp_iv() to summarize and visualize the fit; predict_realloc() for reallocation predictions; fit_check() for residual diagnostics; ilr() for the formula-interface composition marker.

Other composition as predictor: plot.comp_iv(), summary.comp_iv()

Examples

cd <- declare_composition(timeuse, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
                          closure = 1440)
m <- comp_iv(cd, outcome = "obesity", model = "glm", family = "binomial")
m$omnibus
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   term        statistic    df    p.value
#>   <chr>           <dbl> <int>      <dbl>
#> 1 composition      28.9     3 0.00000233

# The full quadratic in the coordinates, a predicted outcome that can curve
curved <- comp_iv(cd, outcome = "zbmi", model = "lm", curvature = TRUE)
curved$omnibus
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   term        statistic    df  p.value
#>   <chr>           <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 composition      310.     9 2.10e-61
